caseOrder: seed, then health control, then policy, in the arrays' order
claimsToTest: The wounded citadel creates understandable recovery pressure alongside a supported immediate counterattack, using normal paid construction and citadel choices.
Regeneration is optional and slow. Whether its actual healing meaningfully offsets delayed offense is unknown; nominal healing alone is not evidence of a useful choice.
Full-health controls test whether the wound changes practical survival margin, losses, completion, or tolerance of the greedy opening. Fixed policies do not establish what a human would choose.
record: every successful paid transaction and failed player attempt
first actual damage/contact and first core damage
initial building losses and their timing
five-second core HP, healing, gold, income and force-count trace
minimum core HP, actual healing, spending, outcome, elapsed time
ordinary economy ledger and final save roundtrip
interpretation: Inspect all twenty cases, including losses. No seed search, automatic retries, heldout claim or best-case-only report.
Check ordinary prices, income, kill gold and no extra funding. The factory authors inherited assets only before tick zero.
Compare the same policy and seed across health controls. These are total-effect controls: ordinary enemy AI may react differently once battles diverge.
Compare recovery and counterattack purchase timing, damage, losses, healing and results. They have different commitments, so this is not an isolated causal estimate of regeneration.
The equal-price arrows-income control tests an alternative to regeneration within the same scripted build order. It is not a mandatory-win or no-regen-loss gate.
A no-regen win is welcome. Idle winning is a warning to inspect pressure, not an automatic rejection. A scripted loss alone does not prove human difficulty.

If the wound only changes the displayed final HP, or recovery heals a token amount without affecting risk or pacing, do not call the recovery choice established. Revise the design or narrow the claim before admission.
No arbitrary HP, healing or win-rate threshold. The reviewer should explain concrete risk, timing or loss differences and limitations.
stop: Stop on source drift, ledger/price error, invalid restore, or coordinator request. Keep partial results outside source and do not retry without review.
nextGates: independent preopen review of exact source and plan
coordinator permission before any gameplay case
independent interpretation and understandable interactive pacing review
wait for canonical Chapter8 fifth mission before unlock or production admission
separate production identity, persistence, catalog, release and aggregate checks
